text:
ana: hi team, new hire question. I'm on Ubuntu 22.04 and after connecting the WireGuard profile, small API GETs work but large POSTs to internal deployments (e.g., POST /upload ~2MB) fail with connection reset. curl shows 'HTTP/1.1 200' for a moment then 'Connection reset by peer'. Any MTU/split-tunnel weirdness?

chris: welcome @ana! this sounds like MTU/fragmentation. Mobile hotspots and some home ISPs MSS/PMTU blackhole on UDP (WireGuard) so large packets die. Can you try lowering the wg0 MTU temporarily?

ana: oops typo - ana. tried `sudo ip link set dev wg0 mtu 1280` and reconnected. still failing, same reset.

julian: try adjusting both MTU and forcing TCP MSS clamping on the host: `sudo iptables -t mangle -A FORWARD -p tcp --tcp-flags SYN,RST SYN -j TCPMSS --clamp-mss-to-pmtu` then restart wg. Also sometimes `mtu 1400` is better than 1280.

ana: applied iptables rule and set mtu 1400. reconnected and retried POST -> success! :tada:

infra-bot: Ticket INF-9234 opened by ana: "WireGuard MTU causing POST resets on Ubuntu" Assigned: chris ETA: 8h

chris: glad that worked. we'll add a short note to the onboarding guide about MTU and the iptables TCPMSS workaround. Also, if you frequently tether, request the full-tunnel tag for your device.

ana: is the iptables rule safe on company-managed laptop? it's persistent across reboots?

julian: iptables rule is fine but not persistent by default. For managed laptops we prefer to push a small systemd service or use nmcli if NetworkManager is present. Eng-infra will coordinate if we need to make it permanent in MDM.

helpdesk: if you want, we can create a temporary session and push a persistent fix. ping helpdesk and include device name ana-laptop-01.

ana: thanks all, posting this to my notes and the onboarding checklist would save others.

infra-bot: Ticket INF-9234 updated: status -> Resolved. Resolution: advised TCPMSS clamp + mtu 1400; doc note added.
